proposed_facts.reason: Canonical collision forwarding and item-drop implementation confirm the ground-loss event and supplied velocity. The item-present branch calls ftCo_80090780, preserving its parasol alternative; the else branch directly calls Fall. Read 'no item remains' as the initial item-presence branch, not a post-drop recheck.
ReleaseHeavyItem meaningfully improves the rendered ReleaseItem name: the helper requires a non-null item and itIsHeavy == 1, unlike the adjacent damage callback.
Independently checked the forwarding wrapper and ft_80085088/ft_800850E0 chain: friction and facing are passed through, x594_b0 selects TransN Z times facing, and both branches apply ground movement.

The complete Lift implementation contains no general ownership-loss exit poll. The external throw selector returns false without an item. Explicit ground-loss dispatch and release behavior support the corrected mechanic mapping.

Entry routines install the non-null-item damage drop callback; the separate cleanup is heavy-only. Item_8026ABD8 invokes dropped handling, and CaptureYoshi calls cleanup before assigning capture associations and changing motion.

All three Lift collision handlers supply this callback to ft_8008403C, which invokes it on failed ground retention. OnGroundLoss describes both item-dependent branches without asserting a single destination.

contradictions.reason: Accept deferral of the three .data claims: the Y setter asserts null/quaternion conditions and the macro stringifies the condition, but neither source establishes anonymous-section attribution or a 37-byte compiled contribution.

Accept deferral of both .sdata claims and all four .sdata2 claims. Local initializers, turn arithmetic and supplied zero vectors do not prove compiled storage type, extent or provenance. The positioning-during-damage interpretation is additionally contradicted by dropped-item dispatch; the supplied vector is consumed as velocity.
Accept superseding the conflated Fall explanation: the two branches have distinct callees, and the item-present callee includes airborne conversion and a parasol exception.

Accept superseding ReleaseItem with ReleaseHeavyItem and replacing the file-level synchronization explanation with release semantics. The two helpers have different guards, and external capture cleanup confirms the reusable lifetime role.
Accept the walk-physics explanation as useful additional knowledge, while explicitly retaining the supported existing forwarding behavior.

Accept removal of the general automatic ownership-loss exit implication. Item absence selects the ground-loss else branch or makes throw selection fail; it is not independently polled to leave Lift. Other supported inherited names, explanations and links remain retained without equivalent rewrites.
